title: FE Exam 2027: 7 Facts Before You Register
description: A concise guide to FE Exam 2027 eligibility, format, fees, disciplines, scoring, and a practical 10-week study plan.

pages.heading: FE Exam 2027: 7 Things to Know
pages.text: Understand the licensing path, eligibility, format, cost and study timeline before you register.
pages.alt: Engineering students planning their FE Exam preparation around blueprints and a laptop

pages.heading: 1. It Starts the PE Path
pages.text: The usual route is degree, FE exam, qualifying experience, PE exam and state licensure. Passing the FE alone does not make you a PE.
pages.alt: Graduate engineer walking toward infrastructure that represents the path to professional licensure

pages.heading: 2. Know the Clock
pages.text: The computer-based exam has 110 questions and 5 hours 20 minutes of exam time within a 6-hour appointment, including a scheduled 25-minute break.
pages.alt: Engineering student taking a computer-based exam at an authorized testing station

pages.heading: 3. Eligibility Is State-Specific
pages.text: The FE is designed mainly for final-year students and recent graduates. Confirm your education and registration rules with your state licensing board.
pages.alt: Engineering students reviewing exam eligibility requirements with an academic adviser

pages.heading: 4. Budget Beyond the Fee
pages.text: NCEES lists a $225 base fee in its 2026 guide. Confirm the 2027 amount, plus possible state-board, travel and approved-calculator costs.
pages.alt: Engineering student budgeting exam costs with a laptop, calculator and study materials

pages.heading: 5. Pick the Right Discipline
pages.text: Choose from seven FE disciplines. Match your degree and the official exam specifications instead of selecting the option that only sounds easiest.
pages.alt: Multidisciplinary engineering laboratory representing the seven FE exam disciplines

pages.heading: 6. There Is No Public Cutoff
pages.text: NCEES reports pass or fail and does not publish a fixed passing score. Recent first-time discipline pass rates cited in the guide range from 61% to 69%.
pages.alt: Engineering graduate checking a pass-or-fail exam result on a laptop

pages.heading: 7. Prepare for 10 Weeks
pages.text: Study the handbook first, then practice by topic, move to mixed sets and finish with timed simulations plus an error log.
pages.alt: Engineering student following a structured study calendar with practice problems and an approved calculator

pages.heading: Register With a Plan
pages.text: Check your board requirements, choose the right discipline, confirm the current fee and schedule the exam around a realistic study timeline.
pages.alt: Engineering students completing a practical FE Exam registration and preparation plan
